html:
German South West Africa was a colony of Germany from 1884 to 1915, in what is now Namibia. The map shows it in 1914.

It began when the merchant Adolf Luderitz bought coastal land at Angra Pequena, and Germany declared a protectorate in 1884. German settlers took the best grazing land of the Herero and Nama peoples. When they rose in 1904, the German commander Lothar von Trotha issued an order to drive the Herero into the desert and kill them. Tens of thousands died of thirst, in battle and in prison camps. The Herero and Nama genocide is often called the first genocide of the 1900s.

Diamonds were found near Luderitz in 1908, and towns such as Kolmanskop sprang up. In World War I South African troops invaded, and the Germans surrendered in 1915. The Union of South Africa then ruled the land under a League of Nations mandate until Namibia's independence in 1990. The port of Walvis Bay was never German.
sum: German South West Africa was a colony of Germany from 1884 to 1915, in what is now Namibia. The map shows it in 1914.
